mainTopic: Aggadic number-meanings, the יצר הרע and יצר טוב, and how כהונה passed to אברהם; then the new chapter on מודר הנאה versus מודר מאכל
overview: This amud starts with אגדה and ends with הלכה. It first finishes a statement that the letters of 'השטן' add up to 364. Then רמי בר אבא teaches that when אברם's name became אברהם (243 became 248), he gained control over all his limbs, including the eyes, the ears and the organ of מילה. He also reads פסוקים in קהלת as a picture of the inner battle: the body is a small city attacked by the יצר הרע, and the 'poor wise man' who saves it is the יצר טוב, through תשובה and good deeds. Next, רבי זכריה in the name of רבי ישמעאל explains that כהונה was meant to come from שם (מלכי צדק). Because he blessed אברהם before blessing God, the כהונה went to אברהם's descendants instead. The chapter ארבעה נדרים then ends. A new משנה teaches that a מודר הנאה and a מודר מאכל differ only in walking on the property and in borrowing utensils not used for food. The גמרא says this משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who forbids even ויתור, and then begins discussing the משנה's rule about lending utensils.

steps.title: The numerical value of 'the Satan' is 364
steps.stepSummary: The letters of the word 'השטן' add up to 364.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'השטן' (the Satan), when you count its letters as numbers, comes out to 364.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a thought that started just before this part of the text. It points out that the letters of 'השטן' add up to 364.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every Hebrew letter has a number value: ה=5, ש=300, ט=9, נ=50, which totals 364. A solar year has 365 days, so 364 is one day short. The usual explanation is that there is one day a year, יום הכיפורים, when the שטן has no power to accuse.

keyTerms.meaning: In its count, meaning its numerical value (like גִּימַטְרִיָּא)

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not start a new discussion. It is the end of a statement that began before this section, so it can feel like it starts in the middle.

phrases.english: "The Satan" — in its numerical value
phrases.notes: Count the letters: ה is 5, ש is 300, ט is 9, נ is 50.

phrases.english: is three hundred and sixty-four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement that began before this section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The letters of השטן equal 364, one less than the days of the year.

steps.title: From אברם to אברהם: rule over 243 limbs, then 248
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר אבא learns from the extra ה in אברהם's name that after his מילה he gained control over 248 limbs instead of 243.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר אבא said: The Torah first calls him 'אברם' and later 'אברהם.' At first, ה׳ made him master over 243 limbs. In the end, ה׳ made him master over 248 limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר אבא brings a new teaching built on letter-numbers. He uses the two names אברם and אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברם adds up to 243 (א=1, ב=2, ר=200, ם=40). Adding a ה (=5) to make אברהם gives 248, the traditional number of limbs in a body. The name change came together with the command of מילה, so the extra ה shows that אברהם gained full control over five more limbs.

keyTerms.meaning: אברהם's name before and after ה׳ changed it
He made him king, meaning He gave him rule or control
At first ... and in the end

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the idea that a person can rule over his body and not be ruled by it, and that the מצוה of מילה completes that control.

phrases.english: And Rami bar Abba said:
It is written "Avram," and it is written "Avraham."
At first, the Holy One, Blessed be He, made him king
over two hundred forty-three limbs,
phrases.notes: That's the number of אברם: א=1, ב=2, ר=200, ם=40.

phrases.english: and in the end He made him king
over two hundred forty-eight limbs,
phrases.notes: The added ה is worth 5, so אברהם comes to 248.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא: כְּתִיב ״אַבְרָם״, וּכְתִיב ״אַבְרָהָם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching by רמי בר אבא, using the same letter-number method as the previous line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name change from אברם (243) to אברהם (248) shows that he went from ruling 243 limbs to ruling all 248.

steps.title: The five limbs that were added
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the five extra limbs: two eyes, two ears, and the tip of the male organ.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the five: two eyes, two ears, and the tip of the organ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which five limbs make up the difference between 243 and 248.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These five are body parts that are hard to control: what the eyes see, what the ears hear, and the organ of desire. After his מילה, אברהם was master over these too. The organ is listed because the מילה is done there.

keyTerms.meaning: The tip of the body, meaning the male organ

steps.whatToRemember: אברם (243) became אברהם (248). The extra five limbs are two eyes, two ears and the organ, all of which אברהם fully controlled after his מילה.

phrases.english: These are they:
two eyes, and two ears,
and the tip of the organ.
phrases.notes: He means the end of the male organ, the place where the מילה is done.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out which five limbs make up the jump from 243 to 248 in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The five added limbs are the two eyes, the two ears and the tip of the organ.

steps.title: The small city under siege: body, limbs, evil inclination, sins
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר אבא reads the first half of a פסוק in קהלת as a picture of the body attacked by the יצר הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר אבא said: What does the verse mean, 'A little city with few men in it...'? 'A little city' is the body. 'Few men in it' are the limbs. 'A great king came against it and surrounded it' is the evil inclination. 'He built traps and siege works against it' are sins.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר אבא gives a third teaching. He explains a פסוק in קהלת as a משל, a parable, about a person's body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each part of the פסוק stands for something inside a person. The body is the city and the limbs are its people. The יצר הרע is the strong king who surrounds the city, and sins are the traps he builds to capture it. This also connects to the last step, since both teachings are about who rules over the limbs.

keyTerms.meaning: What is meant by what is written
Traps and nets, or siege works

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא, מַאי דִּכְתִיב:
phrases.english: And Rami bar Abba said: What is meant by what is written:
"A little city and men, etc."
"A little city" — this is the body;
"and few men in it" — these are the limbs;
"and a great king came against it and surrounded it" —
this is the evil inclination;
"and he built against it traps and nets" —
these are sins.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא, מַאי דִּכְתִיב: ״עִיר קְטַנָּה וַאֲנָשִׁים וְגוֹ׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching by the same speaker, רמי בר אבא, again about the limbs of the body.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the פסוק, the city is the body, its people are the limbs, the great king is the יצר הרע, and the siege traps are sins.

steps.title: The poor wise man: the good inclination that no one remembers
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the פסוק: the poor wise man is the יצר טוב, his wisdom is תשובה and good deeds, and no one remembers him when the יצר הרע is strong.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'There was found in it a poor and wise man' is the good inclination. 'He saved the city with his wisdom' is repentance and good deeds. 'Yet no one remembered that poor man' means that when the evil inclination is in control, nobody remembers the good inclination.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר אבא keeps explaining the same פסוק. Now he turns to the hero of the story, the poor wise man who saves the city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יצר טוב is 'poor' because it seems weak next to the mighty king, but it is wise. It saves the person through תשובה and good deeds. The sad ending of the פסוק is explained too: at the moment the יצר הרע pushes, a person forgets about his יצר טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no one who remembers him

steps.whatToRemember: In the משל from קהלת, the body is a small city attacked by the strong יצר הרע and its traps of sin. The 'poor' but wise יצר טוב can save it through תשובה and good deeds, but in the heat of temptation people forget it is there.

phrases.english: "And there was found in it a poor and wise man" —
this is the good inclination;
"and he saved the city with his wisdom" —
this is repentance and good deeds.

phrases.aramaic: ״וְאָדָם לֹא זָכַר אֶת הָאִישׁ הַמִּסְכֵּן הַהוּא״ —
phrases.english: "Yet no person remembered that poor man" —
meaning that at the time of the evil inclination
there is no one who remembers the good inclination.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וּמָצָא בָהּ אִישׁ מִסְכֵּן וְחָכָם״ — זֶה יֵצֶר טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation of the קהלת פסוק that began in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The poor wise man is the יצר טוב, his saving wisdom is תשובה and good deeds, and when the יצר הרע is strong, no one remembers the יצר טוב.

steps.title: Wisdom is stronger than the body's ten rulers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads another פסוק in קהלת the same way. The 'wisdom' is תשובה and good deeds, and the 'ten rulers' are ten body parts.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Wisdom is a stronghold to the wise man more than ten rulers.' The wisdom is repentance and good deeds. The ten rulers are two eyes, two ears, two hands, two legs, the tip of the male organ, and the mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its reading of קהלת. It explains a new פסוק as describing the battle inside a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, the poor wise man (the יצר טוב) was forgotten when the יצר הרע was strong. This פסוק adds the hopeful side: תשובה and good deeds are stronger than the ten body parts that a person uses to act in the world. The list differs slightly from step 3, because here hands, legs and mouth are included.

keyTerms.meaning: a polite term for the tip of the male organ

steps.whatToRemember: The body's ten 'rulers' can lead a person, but תשובה and good deeds are stronger than all of them.

phrases.english: "Wisdom is a stronghold to the wise man
more than ten rulers."
"Wisdom is a stronghold to the wise man":
this is repentance and good deeds.
"More than ten rulers":
the two eyes, and two ears,
and two hands, and two legs,
and the tip of the organ, and the mouth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same style of reading קהלת as a picture of the inner struggle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תשובה and good deeds overpower the ten body parts that lead a person to act.

steps.title: כהונה was meant for שם but went to אברהם
steps.stepSummary: רבי זכריה, quoting רבי ישמעאל, says הקב״ה wanted כהונה to come from שם. Because שם put אברהם's blessing before God's blessing, the כהונה came through אברהם instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זכריה said in the name of רבי ישמעאל: God wanted the priesthood to come from שם, as it says, 'And he was a priest of God Most High.' Once he put אברהם's blessing before God's blessing, God made it come from אברהם.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. It explains how the כהונה moved from שם's line to אברהם's line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls מלכי צדק (understood here as שם) a כהן, so the plan was for his children to be כהנים. His mistake in the order of the blessings changed the plan. The next steps bring the פסוקים that prove this.

keyTerms.meaning: נח's son, understood here to be מלכי צדק

steps.confusionAlert: 'הוציאה מאברהם' does not mean God took the כהונה away from אברהם. It means God made the כהונה come out through אברהם.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זְכַרְיָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zekharya said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, wanted
to bring out the priesthood from Shem,
as it is stated: "And he was a priest of God Most High."
phrases.notes: בראשית 14:18. 'He' is מלכי צדק, whom the גמרא treats as שם.

phrases.english: Once he put the blessing of Avraham
before the blessing of the Omnipresent,
He brought it out from Avraham.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זְכַרְיָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic, though it is still about אברהם, who appeared in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because מלכי צדק blessed אברהם before God, the כהונה passed to אברהם's descendants.

steps.title: The פסוק shows the blessings in the wrong order
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in בראשית shows that מלכי צדק blessed אברהם first and God second.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And he blessed him and said: Blessed be אברם of God Most High, Maker of heaven and earth, and blessed be God Most High.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the פסוק that shows the mistake mentioned in step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Look at the order inside the פסוק: 'Blessed be Avram' comes before 'blessed be God Most High.' This order is the 'putting first' that step 7 talked about.

phrases.english: As it is stated: "And he blessed him and said:
Blessed be Avram of God Most High,
Maker of heaven and earth,
and blessed be God Most High."
phrases.notes: בראשית 14:19-20. Notice that אברם is blessed before God.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim in step 7 that מלכי צדק put אברהם's blessing first.
steps.raayaObject: That מלכי צדק blessed אברהם before God

steps.title: אברהם objects to the order of the blessings
steps.stepSummary: אברהם asks מלכי צדק how he could bless the servant before the master.
steps.simpleTranslation: אברהם said to him: Does one put the blessing of a servant before the blessing of his master?
steps.whatsHappening: Within the story, אברהם points out what was wrong with the blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם calls himself the 'servant' and God the 'master.' God should have been blessed first. His question names exactly what מלכי צדק did wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: his master (literally, the one who owns him)

phrases.english: Avraham said to him:
And does one put the blessing of a servant
before the blessing of his master?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ אַבְרָהָם וְכִי מַקְדִּימִין בִּרְכַּת עֶבֶד לְבִרְכַּת קוֹנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the objection to the blessing order quoted in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blessing a servant before his master is improper.

steps.title: תהלים shows God gave the כהונה to אברהם
steps.stepSummary: God immediately gave the כהונה to אברהם. This is proven from תהלים קי, which reads 'על דברתי מלכי צדק' as 'because of the words of מלכי צדק.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately God gave it to אברהם, as it says: 'The Lord says to my lord: Sit at My right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool.' And after that it is written: 'The Lord has sworn and will not regret: you are a priest forever, על דברתי מלכי צדק.' This means: because of what מלכי צדק said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that the כהונה went to אברהם. It brings two פסוקים from the same chapter of תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק shows that the chapter speaks about אברהם ('my lord'). The second פסוק says 'you are a כהן forever.' The words 'על דברתי מלכי צדק' are read as 'because of מלכי צדק's speech,' meaning the badly ordered blessing caused the switch.

keyTerms.meaning: read here as 'because of the words of'

phrases.english: Immediately He gave it to Avraham,
as it is stated: "The Lord says to my lord:
phrases.notes: תהלים 110:1. 'My lord' is read as אברהם.

phrases.english: Sit at My right hand
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet,"
and after it is written:
"The Lord has sworn and will not regret:
you are a priest forever
al divrati Malki Tzedek."
phrases.notes: תהלים 110:4. The next line explains what these words mean here.

phrases.english: Because of the speech of Malki Tzedek.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the result of אברהם's objection: the כהונה was given to him.
steps.raayaObject: That the כהונה was given to אברהם because of מלכי צדק's words

steps.title: מלכי צדק was a כהן, but his children were not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the פסוק in בראשית: 'he' was a כהן, meaning only he himself and not his children.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what is written: 'And he was a priest of God Most High.' He was a priest, but his children are not priests.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the topic by showing that the original פסוק already hints at the whole story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, the word 'והוא כהן' was the proof that שם was meant to have the כהונה. Now the extra word 'הוא' is read as a limit: he alone was a כהן. So the same פסוק fits the final outcome too.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what is written

steps.whatToRemember: מלכי צדק (שם) was a כהן himself. Because he blessed אברהם before God, the כהונה went to אברהם's children and not to his own.

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
"And he was a priest of God Most High":
he is a priest, but his children are not priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב וְהוּא כֹהֵן לְאֵל עֶלְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the conclusion back to the פסוק first quoted in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The word 'הוא' limits the כהונה to מלכי צדק personally; his descendants did not inherit it.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter ארבעה נדרים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally closes the chapter called ארבעה נדרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter ארבעה נדרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The chapter ארבעה נדרים ends here, and a new chapter is about to begin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is a closing formula, not an argument. It marks the end of the discussion about מלכי צדק and כהונה and the rest of that chapter. Everything after it starts a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: "We will return to you": the line said when finishing a chapter
"Four vows": the name of the chapter that just ended

phrases.english: We will return to you, "Four Vows"
phrases.notes: A chapter is named after its opening words. This line says goodbye to the chapter that started with "ארבעה נדרים."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter that ended with the reading of the פסוק about מלכי צדק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter ארבעה נדרים is complete; a new chapter follows.

steps.title: The only differences between a full benefit vow and a food vow
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה says a מודר הנאה and a מודר מאכל differ only in walking on the property and in borrowing utensils not used for food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The only difference between someone forbidden by vow from all benefit from his fellow and someone forbidden only from his fellow's food is walking on his property and using utensils that are not used to prepare food.
steps.whatsHappening: The new chapter opens with a משנה comparing two kinds of vows and saying they differ in only two things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מודר הנאה is forbidden every kind of benefit, so he may not even walk on the other person's land or borrow his non-food utensils. A מודר מאכל is forbidden only food-related benefit, so those two things are allowed for him. In every other respect the two vows work the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone forbidden by vow from getting any benefit from another person
Someone forbidden by vow only from another person's food
Setting foot on or walking across someone's property
Food preparation, literally "food for the soul"

steps.confusionAlert: "אין בין" really does mean the two vows are the same in every way except these two items. In those two items the full benefit vow is stricter: the מודר הנאה is forbidden them, while the מודר מאכל is allowed. Everything a מודר מאכל may not do, a מודר הנאה also may not do.

phrases.english: There is no difference between one forbidden by vow from benefiting from his fellow
and one forbidden by vow from his food
except setting foot [on his property]

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵלִים שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין בָּהֶם אוֹכֶל נֶפֶשׁ
phrases.english: and utensils with which one does not prepare food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בֵּין הַמּוּדָּר הֲנָאָה מֵחֲבֵירוֹ לַמּוּדָּר הֵימֶנּוּ מַאֲכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מודר הנאה is forbidden to walk on his fellow's land and to borrow his non-food utensils; a מודר מאכל is permitted both.

steps.title: Which items may be lent to someone under a food vow
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives examples: food-making tools may not be lent to a מודר מאכל, but clothing and jewelry may.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone forbidden by vow from his fellow's food may not be lent a sieve, a strainer, a millstone or an oven. But he may be lent a shirt, a ring, a cloak or nose rings.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues by giving practical examples of the rule it just stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sieves, strainers, millstones and ovens are used to make food, so lending them counts as food benefit and is forbidden to a מודר מאכל. Clothing and jewelry have nothing to do with food, so he may borrow them. A מודר הנאה could not borrow even these.

phrases.english: One forbidden by vow from his fellow's food
[his fellow] may not lend him a sieve or a strainer
or a millstone or an oven
but he may lend him a shirt or a ring
or a cloak or nose rings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the general rule of Step 13 to specific items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food-preparation tools may not be lent to a מודר מאכל; non-food items like clothing and jewelry may.

steps.title: Whose view does this משנה follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking which תנא taught this משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Who is the תנא who taught this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking whose opinion the משנה represents. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids a מודר הנאה even to walk on his fellow's land, which seems very strict. So the גמרא wants to know which sage holds such a strict view.

keyTerms.meaning: "Who taught it?": asking which sage a משנה follows

phrases.english: Gemara
Who taught [this משנה]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the author of the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a מודר הנאה may not even walk on his fellow's property.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: It is רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה answers that the משנה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: It is רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה names רבי אליעזר as the author of the משנה. The source for this comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer ties the משנה to one specific sage. It suggests the strict rule about walking on property may not be everyone's view.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the question
The תנא whose view the משנה follows

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said
It is Rabbi Eliezer

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא

steps.title: רבי אליעזר forbids even things people normally let go
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי אליעזר holds that even ויתור is forbidden to a מודר הנאה, which explains the משנה's rule about walking on property.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אליעזר says: Even something people normally let go of is forbidden to someone under a benefit vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that the משנה matches רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking across someone's land is the kind of thing owners usually don't mind, called ויתור. Only רבי אליעזר forbids even this to a מודר הנאה. So the משנה, which forbids walking on the land, must follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: "As it was taught": introduces a ברייתא
Something people normally let others have without minding

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule that a מודר הנאה may not walk on his fellow's land follows רבי אליעזר. He forbids even ויתור, small benefits that owners don't normally care about.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the משנה's strict rule on walking on property depends on one sage's view about ויתור.

phrases.english: as it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says
Even something people let go of is forbidden for one under a benefit vow.
phrases.notes: "ויתור" means things owners normally don't mind others doing, like walking across their field.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר אֲפִילּוּ וִיתּוּר אָסוּר בְּמוּדַּר הֲנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אדא בר אהבה's answer in Step 16 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה (forbidding דריסת הרגל to a מודר הנאה) follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי אליעזר rules that even ויתור is forbidden to a מודר הנאה.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה's line about lending to a מודר מאכל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the משנה's rule about what may not be lent to a מודר מאכל. This sets up a new discussion of that rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: someone who is forbidden by vow from getting food benefit from his friend, the friend may not lend him, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the next line of the משנה as a heading. It is setting up a new discussion about lending utensils to a מודר מאכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 15-17 dealt with the first difference in the משנה, walking on the property. Now the גמרא moves to the second part: which utensils the friend may not lend. The word וכו׳ tells us the rest of the משנה's line is meant, even though it is not written out here.

keyTerms.meaning: A person forbidden by vow from getting food benefit from someone
And so on: the rest of the quoted line

phrases.english: One who is forbidden by vow from food of his friend
he may not lend him, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמּוּדָּר מַאֲכָל מֵחֲבֵירוֹ לֹא יַשְׁאִילֶנּוּ וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the walking-on-property rule, explained in steps 15-17, to the משנה's rule about lending utensils.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A food-making utensil may not be lent to someone who is a מודר מאכל from the lender.
